package_info.why_malicious: commons-collections version 3.2.1 contains a critical, well-documented deserialization vulnerability (CVE-2015-6420) that allows remote code execution when untrusted serialized data is processed. This vulnerability is widely exploited and is considered a severe risk by security professionals and automated scanning tools.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when the application deserializes user-supplied input
execution_context.file_location: core library code (commons-collections 3.2.1), specifically classes such as org.apache.commons.collections.functors.InvokerTransformer

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Vulnerable deserialization logic in commons-collections 3.2.1 that allows remote code execution via crafted serialized objects. Specifically, the InvokerTransformer and related classes can be leveraged in a gadget chain to execute arbitrary commands when deserialized by ObjectInputStream.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code deserializes attacker-controlled input using ObjectInputStream, which triggers a gadget chain (e.g., InvokerTransformer) that results in arbitrary command execution on the host system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Deserializing untrusted data using ObjectInputStream without validation enables attackers to supply malicious serialized objects that exploit known gadget chains, leading to arbitrary code execution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal library code should only deserialize trusted data and must not allow untrusted input to trigger code execution. The presence of insecure deserialization logic and exploitable gadget classes violates secure coding standards and exposes critical attack surfaces.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Deserialization is legitimate when restricted to trusted, validated sources and when using safe object graphs without known gadget chains.
key_indicators: Use of ObjectInputStream to deserialize untrusted input
Presence of InvokerTransformer and related gadget classes in the classpath
No input validation or deserialization whitelisting

attack_chain.action: Application includes commons-collections 3.2.1 and exposes a deserialization endpoint that accepts serialized Java objects from external sources.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker identifies the vulnerable endpoint and prepares a malicious serialized payload.

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a crafted serialized object containing a gadget chain (e.g., using InvokerTransformer) to the vulnerable endpoint.
attack_chain.leads_to: The application deserializes the payload, triggering the gadget chain.

attack_chain.action: The gadget chain executes arbitrary code on the server, such as spawning a shell or initiating outbound network connections.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: remote code execution and potential full system compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Deserialization of untrusted data using ObjectInputStream
Instantiation or invocation of org.apache.commons.collections.functors.InvokerTransformer or similar gadget classes during deserialization
Unexpected invocation of java.lang.Runtime.exec() or similar APIs as a result of deserialization
Process creation or outbound network activity immediately following deserialization
file_indicators: Presence of commons-collections-3.2.1.jar in application dependencies
References to org/apache/commons/collections/functors/InvokerTransformer.class or related gadget classes in the deployed codebase
network_indicators: Inbound HTTP requests containing Java serialized object payloads to endpoints that accept serialized data
Outbound network connections initiated by the application process shortly after deserialization events
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan application dependencies for commons-collections version 3.2.1 or other known vulnerable versions. Monitor for deserialization of untrusted data, especially on network-exposed endpoints. Use runtime instrumentation or security agents to detect instantiation of known gadget classes (e.g., InvokerTransformer) and invocation of process execution APIs during deserialization. Flag any use of vulnerable classes or patterns associated with insecure deserialization. Correlate inbound serialized payloads with subsequent process or network activity to identify exploitation attempts.
